We identified A. xylosoxidans sequence in 4/13 patients and in 4/10 controls.

33824437.citation: Liu et al. Prospective comparison of metagenomic next-generation sequencing and conventional testing for CNS infections after allogeneic HSCT (Nanfang Hospital, China), 2021
33824437.study_design: Prospective cohort (diagnostic-accuracy comparison of mNGS vs conventional testing)

population.population_description: 53 allo-HSCT recipients presenting with CNS disorders (from 567 patients undergoing allo-HSCT); 35 with CNS infection, 11 noninfectious CNS causes, 7 undetermined

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS performed by Beijing Genomics Institute per manufacturer protocol
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA and RNA (viruses' DNA/RNA; detailed criteria in supplementary appendix)

33824437.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis criteria: proven (neurological manifestations + pathogen identified in CSF + histopathology if needed) or probable CNS infection (neurological manifestations, absence of noninfectious aetiology, good response to antimicrobial treatment)

comparator_2x2.against: conventional testing vs final clinical diagnosis; mNGS sensitivity 97.1% (34/35), specificity 94.4% (17/18)

diagnostic_yield.basis: 35/53 patients diagnosed with CNS infection; viruses 28, bacteria 2, fungi 1, mixed 3, unknown 1

33824437.additional_yield_vs_conventional: Among 35 CNS infections, mNGS identified 5 patients not identified by conventional testing; 6 pathogens detected by mNGS only (EBV, HHV-7, HSV-1, S. pneumoniae, R. felis, Aspergillus), 5 of 6 validated
33824437.therapy_change: Treatments given based on aetiology; of 34 CNS-infection patients treated, 24 good response and survived, 9 died of progressing CNS infection, 1 died of severe pneumonia
33824437.mortality_or_outcomes: 9/34 CNS-infection patients died of progressing CNS infection; 1-year and 2-year cumulative incidence of CNS infections 5.51% (95% CI 3.83–7.61%) and 6.59% (95% CI 4.65–8.96%)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: reference standard partly incorporates treatment response and pathogen detection; Sanger/PCR validation of mNGS-only findings creates incorporation risk

33824437.quadas2_notes: All enrolled received both index and comparator (paired CSF testing). Reference standard is clinical (proven/probable criteria), acceptable but partially incorporates treatment response. mNGS-positive-only findings were validated by Sanger/PCR — incorporation bias risk. A single mNGS-only Aspergillus deemed false positive.

evidence_quotes.quote: A total of 53 in the 567 patients undergoing allo-HSCT between July 2016 and March 2019 were enrolled in this prospective study.
A total of 35 patients were diagnosed as CNS infections, including 28 viral, 2 bacterial, 1 fungal, 3 mixed infections, and 1 infection with unknown pathogen.

Among these 35 patients with CNS infections, mNGS identified 5 patients who were not identified by conventional testing. For the remaining 30 infections, mNGS made concurrent diagnoses with conventional testing in 29, while 1 was diagnosed according to the good response to the antimicrobial treatment without etiological evidence.

The sensitivity of mNGS and conventional testing for diagnosing CNS infections post transplant were 97.1% and 82.9%, respectively (P = 0.106), while the specificity of mNGS and conventional testing were 94.4% and 100%, respectively (P = 1.000).
Aspergillus was considered false positive for lack of validation via PCR as well as galactomannan detection in CSF sample.
The methods for pathogens detection in CSF included conventional testing and mNGS. ... mNGS was performed by the Beijing Genomics Institute according to the manufacturer's protocol.

Of the patients with CNS infections, 24 had good response to the treatments and survived, while 9 died because of CNS infections progressing and 1 died of severe pneumonia although with improving CNS disorders on the third day of treatment.
Etiology was identified in 46 of the 53 patients enrolled including CNS infections in 35 (66.0%) and noninfectious causes in 11 (20.8%) patients.

34595132.quadas2_notes: Retrospective, single centre, n=20. No independent 2x2 vs final diagnosis reported; final infection classification is co-defined by mNGS positivity, so diagnostic accuracy cannot be estimated. Yield data usable. Adult and paediatric (median age 12).

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 20 patients with CNS symptoms who received AD-HSCT at the Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Zhengzhou University between February 2019 and December 2020.
A total of 29 tests were performed with 21 of them being positive.

Of the five negative patients, three were diagnosed with a posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, one as having transplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy, and one with transient seizure caused by hypertension. Fifteen patients tested positive, of which four had single infections and eleven had mixed infections.
Five cases of fungal infections, six cases of bacterial infections, and 13 cases of viral infections were detected.
Thirteen patients tested positive for virus while the qPCR detection method of 6 identical specimens were below the minimum detection limit(<1×10 3  U/ml).
According to the protocol of the BGISEQ-200 sequencing platform, the DNA library was constructed through DNA fragmentation, end-repair, adapter-ligation, and PCR amplification.
Twelve patients died, and the main cause of death was a nervous system infection in 10 patients, and severe pneumonia and organ failure in two patients. Eight patients survived.
The survival rate of patients without CNS infection was 80% (4/5), and the survival rate of patients with CNS infection was only 26.7% (4/15).

34595132.exclusion_reason: No 2x2 vs independent reference standard; reference classification incorporates mNGS results (circularity). n=20 patients, retrospective, yield-only data usable.

population.population_description: Adults (≥20 y) with haematologic malignancies and clinical sepsis (qSOFA criteria); infections: pneumonia 9/24 (37.5%), intra-abdominal 7/24 (29.2%), BSI 3/24 (12.5%), UTI 2/24 (8.4%); 14/24 neutropenic

diagnostic_yield.basis: per-patient categories: 9 conventional equal to mNGS, 10 mNGS-only (additional pathogens), 3 conventional-only, 2 inconsistent; most mNGS detections were viruses

evidence_quotes.quote: From June 2019 to December 2019, we conducted a prospected study at National Taiwan University Hospital, which is a tertiary medical center with 2400-beds, located in northern Taiwan.
Fourteen (58.3%) patients were diagnosed with neutropenia (absolute white blood cell < 500 cells/mm 3 ) when sepsis developed.

Of 24 patients enrolled, mNGS and conventional diagnostic methods (blood cultures, serology testing and virus RT-PCR) reached comparable positive results in 9 cases. Of ten patients, mNGS was able to identify additional pathogens compared with conventional methods; most of the pathogens were virus.
Overall, CMV were detected among seven patients by mNGS; only three patients were confirmed with CMV viremia by conventional viral PCR.
Blood test for mNGS was performed within 24 h after the onset of a hypotension episode.

the results of mNGS were not timely available due to high cost and time-consuming data interpretation. Therefore, the impact of mNGS methods on the physicians' preference of antimicrobial agent administration remained unclear.
eight (35.7%) of 14 neutropenic patients obtain equal or more microbiologic evidence via mNGS, and of which five patients were documented with polymicrobial infection.

34835435.exclusion_reason: No 2x2 vs reference standard; comparison categories are relative to conventional testing only (yield-only).

population.population_description: 101 paediatric allo-HSCT recipients with 54 BALF, 32 blood and 15 CSF samples; 87 diagnosed with post-transplant infectious disease, 14 with non-infectious disease; median age at transplant 72 months (5–168); 61 tested within 3 months of HSCT

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS performed by BGI PathoGenesis Pharmaceutical Technology (BGI-Shenzhen) and Hugobiotech Co. Ltd., Beijing, per manufacturer protocol; criteria in supplementary appendix
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA and RNA (not further specified in retrieved text)

35509305.reference_standard: Composite clinical diagnosis: bloodstream infections per NHSN criteria plus final diagnosis based on clinical manifestations, pathogen detection by conventional testing AND mNGS, treatment effect; pulmonary infection based on symptoms, imaging, conventional and NGS detection, rapid on-site evaluation, histopathology, expert opinion, treatment effect; CNS infection per Schmidt-Hieber proven/probable criteria

comparator_2x2.against: conventional pathogen detection vs final diagnosis (sensitivity mNGS 89.7% vs 21.8%; specificity 78.5% vs 92.9%; PPV 96.3 vs 95.0; NPV 55.0 vs 15.0); TP/FN/TN/FP back-derived from reported percentages with denominators 87 infected and 14 non-infected (78/87=89.7%, 11/14=78.5%)

diagnostic_yield.basis: 82.2% of 101 specimens from infected patients: BALF 44/48 (91.7%) mNGS-positive, blood 24/28 (85.7%), CSF 10/11 (90.9%)

35509305.additional_yield_vs_conventional: pulmonary: 33 pathogens mNGS-only vs 11 by both; blood: 19 patients mNGS-positive only vs 5 by both and 1 conventional-only; CSF: 8 pathogens mNGS-only vs 2 by both
35509305.therapy_change: Treatments given based on pathogens; 40/48 pulmonary and 27/28 blood-infection patients responded well; empirical treatment for unclear pathogens
35509305.mortality_or_outcomes: Died: 2 of pulmonary infection progression, 2 of TMA, 2 of aGVHD, 1 of multiple organ failure (blood infection group), 1 of progressing CNS infection (Mucor) and multiple organ failure

Specificity analysis limited by only 14 non-infected cases (authors note this). 2x2 integers back-derived from reported sens/spec percentages and denominators 87/14 — flagged as derived, not verbatim counts.

evidence_quotes.quote: In this study, we traced the records of 101 pediatric recipients with allo-HSCT to investigate the pathogens of infection, and collected 54 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, 32 blood, and 15 cerebrospinal fluid samples. In these samples, 87 was with post-transplant infection and 14 without infection.

mNGS was more sensitive (89.7%) than conventional pathogen detection (21.8%), with a difference of 67.9% (P < 0.001), However, mNGS was less specific (78.5%) than traditional methods (92.9%), with a difference of 14.4% (P = 0.596).

The sensitivity of mNGS for diagnosing pulmonary infections, bloodstream infections or viremia, and CNS infections post-transplant were 91.7, 85.7, and 90.9%, respectively. In contrast, the sensitivity of conventional testing for diagnosing pulmonary infections, bloodstream infections or viremia, and CNS infections post-transplant were 22.9, 21.4, and 18.2%, respectively.
The PPV and NPV of mNGS were 96.3 and 55.0%, respectively. In comparison, the PPV and NPV of traditional pathogen detection were 95.0 and 15.0%, respectively.
For this study, the final diagnosis of bloodstream infections was made based on clinical manifestations, pathogen detection by traditional testing methods and mNGS, and treatment effect observations.

Among the 28 blood specimens of patients with bloodstream infections or viremia, five patients were tested positive by both mNGS and conventional methods, nineteen were positive by mNGS, and one was positive by conventional testing only.
Two pathogens were identified by mNGS and conventional testing both and eight by mNGS only.

Twenty-seven of the patients with bloodstream infections or viremia responded well during the treatments, while one died of multiple organ failure. Ten of the patients with CNS infections had a good response to the treatments, while one died because of CNS infections progressing (the pathogen of the patient was Mucor) and multiple organ failure.
mNGS was performed by the BGI PathoGenesis Pharmaceutical Technology, BGI-Shenzhen and Hugobiotech Co., Ltd., Beijing, China according to the manufacturer's protocol.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively reviewed 73 pediatric patients with HM and pulmonary infection at the pediatric hematology department, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University from January 2020 to October 2021. With our inclusion criteria, 55 pediatric patients were enrolled for this study.
The positive rate of pathogens detected by mNGS was 87.3% (48 of 55 patients), thus by conventional microbiological assays was only 34.5% (19 of 55 patients) (P <0.001).

The overall positivity rate and the rate of mixed infections were 34.5% (19/55) and 7.3% (4/55) only using conventional microbiologic testing. Notably, they increased to 90.9% (50/55) and 30.9% (17/55) when combined with mNGS results, respectively.
bacteria, viruses, fungi and MP were detected in 17/55 (30.9%), 25/55 (45.5%), 19/55 (34.5%) and 2/55 (3.6%) cases by mNGS, respectively
Of the 55 pediatric patients, 31 had neutropenia (56.4%).

the workflow from patient sample to results was completed within 24 hours, saving precious time for these critically ill patients. Specifically, the BALF were separately sent to clinical microbiology laboratories within 2 h for analyses, followed by 1 h for nucleic acid extraction from the genome, 15 h for library preparation and sequencing, and 6 h for bioinformatics analyses and reporting.
The remaining 19 cases were partly covered or not covered by antibiotics before the pathogens were detected, and all these cases adjusted their antibiotics after the pathogens were detected.

35837537.neutropenic_status: FN defined as absolute neutrophil count (ANC) <0.5 × 10^9/L; non-FN ANC >0.5 × 10^9/L

A total of 102 patients were FN, and the remaining 90 patients were non-FN who did not develop neutropenia but had a fever.

the pathogen detection rate of mNGS was significantly higher than the traditional method (80.21% vs 25.00%, P <0.001). And it has obvious advantages in detecting mixed pathogens infection (80.21% vs 4.17%, P <0.001).

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS-positive for Aspergillus in 11/12 pulmonary aspergillosis and 6/21 non-pulmonary aspergillosis patients; 13 putative mixed infections identified, co-pathogens detected in 84.6%

35979088.additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS sensitivity 91.7% vs conventional etiological methods 33.3% and serum (1,3)-β-D-glucan 33.3%
35979088.therapy_change: Based on mNGS results, antimicrobial therapy was altered in 91.7% of patients: 58.4% had agents/spectrum adjusted, 50% started anti-Aspergillus drugs, 16.7% started TMP-SMZ, 25% started anti-viral drugs

quality_flags.overlap_risk: case selection based on mNGS positivity (only patients with fungi identified by mNGS enrolled) — verification bias inflates sensitivity; reference diagnosis uses treatment response

35979088.quadas2_notes: Case-control-style selection: enrolment required a positive mNGS fungal result, then classified by clinical diagnosis — high risk of spectrum/verification bias; accuracy not generalizable to unselected immunocompromised patients. NOT a haemato-oncology population (excluded neutropenic; mostly COPD/diabetes/solid tumors) — limited relevance for our pooled analysis.

evidence_quotes.quote: In this retrospective study, we successively enrolled 33 non-neutropenic patients whose mNGS results (BALF and/or blood and/or pleural fluid samples) identified fungi (e.g., Aspergillus, P. jirovecii, Candida, and Cryptococcus) and were admitted to the Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine of Second Affiliated Hospital, Naval Medical University (Shanghai, China), from June 1, 2018, to January 31, 2022.
Finally, 12 patients were diagnosed with pulmonary aspergillosis, and 21 were diagnosed with non-pulmonary aspergillosis.

mNGS managed to reach a sensitivity of 91.7% for diagnosing pulmonary aspergillosis, which was significantly higher than that of conventional etiological methods (33.3%) and serum (1,3)-β-D-glucan (33.3%).

based on the mNGS results, antimicrobial therapy was altered in 91.7% of patients, 58.4% had the antimicrobial agents or spectrum adjusted, 50% were started with anti-Aspergillus drugs, 16.7% were started with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ), and 25% were started with anti-viral drugs.

The combined clinical diagnosis of pulmonary aspergillosis or non-pulmonary aspergillosis was made by two medical doctors based on host risk factors, clinical symptoms, chest computed tomography images, laboratory findings, and response to treatment.

Patients were excluded from the study based on the following criteria: (1) age <18 years; (2) neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count <1.5×10 9 /L); (3) mNGS not performed; and (4) incomplete medical records.

This method showed satisfactory performance in identifying co-pathogens (84.6%), among which Aspergillus-bacteria, Aspergillus-bacteria-fungi, and Aspergillus-bacteria- P. jirovecii (PJP)-virus were most common.

36034963.citation: Li Wenzi, Zhu Hua, Wen Li, et al. Application Value of Metagenomics Next-Generation Sequencing (mNGS) in Detection of Mucormycosis after Chemotherapy in Children with Acute Leukemia. Evidence-based Complementary and Alternative Medicine, 2022.

population.population_description: Children with acute leukemia who developed mucormycosis after chemotherapy, diagnosed by mNGS; all were in agranulocytosis state during infection
population.haemato_subtypes: 6 ALL, 1 AML

36034963.neutropenic_status: All 7 in agranulocytosis; duration 45 days in the AML case, 8-18 days in ALL cases

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS (platform not specified)

36034963.reference_standard: mNGS itself was the diagnostic basis in all 7 patients; one case confirmed by postoperative pathology (hexamine silver staining of resected lung lobe); conventional tests (blood/sputum culture, fungal smear, GM, G) were negative in all

diagnostic_yield.basis: 7/7 patients mNGS-positive for Mucorales (Rhizopus microsporus, R. delemar, Rhizomucor pusillus, Cunninghamella bertholletiae); no denominator of tested-suspected patients - all enrolled were mNGS-positive

36034963.additional_yield_vs_conventional: All conventional microbiological tests (blood culture, sputum culture, sputum fungal smear, GM, G test) negative in all 7 children; only mNGS identified the pathogen in all cases; 1/7 had positive hexamine-silver staining on resected lung
36034963.turnaround_time: 1-2 days from specimen submission to mNGS report; time from symptom onset to pathogen diagnosis 2-15 days (mean 7.85 days)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single-center pediatric case series; all patients selected because they were mNGS-positive (incorporation/selection bias)

36034963.quadas2_notes: Case series with no comparator cohort and no consecutive sampling of suspected infections; mNGS used as diagnostic criterion (incorporation bias); patient flow diagram (reference 6) not reported; QUADAS-2 risk of bias high in patient selection and reference standard.

evidence_quotes.quote: To retrospectively analyze the clinical data of 7 patients with acute leukemia combined with trichomoniasis after chemotherapy in the department of hematology and oncology of Hebei Children's Hospital
In this study, we retrospectively analyzed seven children with acute leukemia who had early infection detected by the mNGS method after chemotherapy for leukemia from January 2020 to December 2021

There were 6 males and 1 female. ... 6 cases of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and 1 case of acute myeloid leukemia. ... All 7 patients ... were in agranulocytosis state during the course of the disease. The blood culture, sputum culture, sputum fungal smear, galactomannan (GM test) and 1,3 β D glucan (G test) were all negative.

In our study, blood cultures, sputum cultures, fungal smears in sputum, G and GM tests were negative in all children sent for examination. Only one case of resected diseased lung lobe was positive for hexosamine-silver staining
In all cases, it took only 1–2 days from specimen submission to report the test results.
The time from symptom onset to diagnosis of pathogenic bacteria in 7 cases was 2–15 days, with an average of 7.85 days.
After treatment, 1 case died, 2 cases were cured, and 4 cases improved.
In our study, we used the mNGS assay to obtain evidence of pathogenic bacteria by infecting children with PB, BAL, and CSF. Four different mucus genera were identified

36034963.exclusion_reason: Small single-arm case series (n=7); all patients enrolled were mNGS-positive (no suspected-infection denominator); no reference standard independent of mNGS; no comparator 2x2 possible.

36189372.citation: Zhang Qing, Liu Xingchen, Liu Yanyan, et al. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, 2022.
36189372.study_design: Case report (2 cases) plus literature review
36189372.study_period: June 2021 to February 2022 (case 1 admitted 27 June 2021; case 2 admitted 18 October 2021)

population.haemato_subtypes: 1 T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (10-year-old girl), 1 chronic lymphocytic leukemia (64-year-old man on ibrutinib)

36189372.neutropenic_status: Case 1 febrile neutropenia with ANC 0.02 x 10^9/L during induction; case 2 not neutropenic (ANC 21.15 x 10^9/L)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS on MGISEQ-2000 (MGI, Shenzhen); Genskey library kit; ~12,000-genome database

36189372.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis confirmed by fungal culture of local secretions (case 1: fluorescent staining of nasal secretions showing pauci-septate hyphae + multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis; case 2: secretion culture grew Mucor)

diagnostic_yield.basis: 2/2 PB mNGS positive for Mucorales (Lichtheimia ramosa 3330 reads; Mucor irregularis 55 reads)

36189372.additional_yield_vs_conventional: Initial blood/secretion cultures and G/GM tests were negative before mNGS; mNGS preceded culture confirmation; 'Within 48 h, the mNGS results were released' while subsequent secretion culture confirmed
36189372.therapy_change: Case 1: switched to amphotericin B cholesterol sulfate complex + nasal amphotericin + debridement; case 2: antifungal adjusted to ABCD after mNGS, plus ganciclovir
36189372.mortality_or_outcomes: Both patients recovered ('both patients obtained successful outcomes'); no return of mucormycosis until Feb 2022 (case 1); skin wound completely healed (case 2)

36189372.quadas2_notes: n=2; no applicability for pooled diagnostic accuracy; reference standard partly clinical (multidisciplinary diagnosis) plus culture.

evidence_quotes.quote: Here we used mNGS to timely diagnose an infection with Lichtheimia ramosa and Mucor irregularis in two patients with hematologic malignancies
Within 48 h, the mNGS results were released: M. irregularis, human betaherpesvirus, human alphaherpesvirus, and Alphatorquevirus were detected
Fungus | Lichtheimia | 3414 | Lichtheimia ramosa | 3330 ... 2 | PB | Fungus | Mucor | 55 | Mucor irregularis | 55
The subsequent fungal culture of the secretion revealed Mucor growth, confirming the cutaneous mucormycosis.
Following treatment with amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate complex, the symptoms were reduced significantly, and both patients obtained successful outcomes.

36189372.exclusion_reason: Case report (n=2 patients, below threshold); no 2x2 or yield denominator.

36211959.citation: Zhang Binglei, Gui Ruirui, Wang Qian, et al. Comparing the application of mNGS after combined pneumonia in hematologic patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or chemotherapy. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, 2022.

population.population_description: Hematologic patients with respiratory symptoms, poor empirical anti-infective response and difficult sputum sampling who received BALF mNGS; 41 allo-HSCT recipients and 43 chemotherapy patients
population.haemato_subtypes: Transplant group: 26 AML, 10 ALL, 2 AA, 3 CMML. Chemotherapy group: 14 AML, 7 ALL, 10 NHL, 9 MM, 2 AA, 1 CLL

36211959.neutropenic_status: Not reported as a stratification variable

specimens.type: BALF conventional methods (culture, G test, GM test, qPCR)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS on MGISEQ-200 (50 bp single-end); Nanjing Practice Medicine library kits; Kraken2 vs in-house NCBI-derived database

36211959.reference_standard: None independent of mNGS - comparison was mNGS positivity vs conventional test positivity; final clinical adjudication not used as reference standard

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS positive 47/48 tests (97.9%) in transplantation group and 41/45 tests (91.1%) in chemotherapy group; conventional methods positive 8/41 (19.5%) and 6/43 (14.0%) of patients respectively. Note: 48 + 45 = 93 mNGS tests. Positivity is detection rate, not accuracy vs a clinical reference standard.

36211959.additional_yield_vs_conventional: Detection rate of mNGS significantly higher than conventional in both groups (97.9% vs 19.5% transplantation; 91.1% vs 14.0% chemotherapy; all P<0.05); mixed infections common (mNGS mixed pathogens 39/47 transplant, 29/41 chemotherapy tests)
36211959.therapy_change: Anti-infective treatment guided by pathogen results; respiratory symptoms improved in 30/40 transplant and 37/39 chemotherapy patients
36211959.mortality_or_outcomes: 13 deaths in transplant group (10 mainly from severe pneumonia/respiratory failure), 12 deaths in chemotherapy group (2 from severe pneumonia); death due to pulmonary infection 76.9% vs 16.7% (P=0.003)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Same BALF specimen split for conventional tests and mNGS (paired); 3 patients had 2-3 mNGS tests (non-independent tests); no clinical reference standard, so 'positivity' may include colonization

36211959.quadas2_notes: No independent reference standard; QUADAS-2 risk of bias high for reference standard (mNGS positivity vs conventional positivity, not clinical diagnosis). Some counting inconsistencies in the paper (41/43 patients vs 48/45 tests).

evidence_quotes.quote: Here, we describe the use of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage (BALF) fluid to identify pathogens in patients with hematologic comorbid respiratory symptoms in a retrospective study with 84 patients.

We retrospectively analyzed the clinical characteristics of 84 patients with respiratory symptoms who received allo-HSCT and/or chemotherapy at the Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Zhengzhou University and the Third People's Hospital of Zhengzhou from April 2020 to April 2022.

In the transplantation group, 8 cases (19.5%) and 47 cases (97.9%) were positive for BALF by conventional method detection and mNGS detection, respectively, and 6 cases (14.0%) and 41 cases (91.1%) in chemotherapy group, respectively. The detection rate of mNGS in both groups was significantly higher than that of conventional detection methods (all P<0.05).

In the transplantation and chemotherapy groups, 41 and 43 tests were performed by conventional methods, respectively, and 48 (3 tests in 2 patients and 2 tests in 3 patients) and 45 (2 tests in 1 patient) tests were performed by mNGS, respectively.
Qualified DNBs were loaded into the flow cell and sequenced (50 bp, single-end) on the MGISEQ-200 platform.

TIANamp Micro DNA Kit (DP316, TIANGEN Biotech, Beijing, China) and QIAamp Viral RNA Mini Kit RNA extraction kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) were used for DNA or RNA extraction according to the manufacturers' recommendation, respectively.
The proportion of death due to pulmonary infection was significantly higher in the transplantation group than in the chemotherapy group (76.9% vs 16.7%, χ2 = 9.077, P=0.003)

Among 40 infected patients in the transplantation group, 30 had improved respiratory symptoms after treatment and 10 had no significant improvement, and among 39 patients in the chemotherapy group, 37 had significant improvement in symptoms after treatment and 2 had no significant improvement.

36531828.citation: Tao Huan, Hua Fang, Chen Yingying, et al. Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing (mNGS) for the Timely Diagnosis of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Infection in Leukemia Patients: A Report of Two Cases. Case Reports in Infectious Diseases, 2022.

population.haemato_subtypes: 1 acute myelogenous leukemia (24-year-old man), 1 acute monocytic leukemia (54-year-old man)

36531828.neutropenic_status: Febrile neutropenia after first chemotherapy in both; case 1 WBC 0.16 x 10^9/L, neutrophil count 0

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS (platform not detailed in text)

36531828.reference_standard: Blood culture (case 2: CrKP grew 4 days after mNGS) and clinical response; stool cultures showed CrKP colonization

diagnostic_yield.basis: Case 2 blood mNGS positive K. pneumoniae 225 unique reads at 16 h; case 1 CrKP bacteremia confirmed via stool culture/blood culture per narrative; CSF mNGS detected Aspergillus flavus (62 reads) and CMV (218 reads) with negative culture

36531828.additional_yield_vs_conventional: In case 2, mNGS revealed K. pneumoniae after 16 hours while blood culture showed CrKP after 4 days; CSF mNGS detected A. flavus and CMV while 'the culture was negative'
36531828.therapy_change: Zavicefta (ceftazidime-avibactam) given immediately based on mNGS; voriconazole started for intracranial fungal infection
36531828.mortality_or_outcomes: Both patients improved ('After treatment, the patient's body temperature and blood pressure returned to normal'; headache relieved)

36531828.quadas2_notes: n=2; anecdotal; no denominators; QUADAS-2 not applicable for pooling.

evidence_quotes.quote: Herein, we report two leukemia patients who developed severe infections due to carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CrKP).
Sixteen hours later, mNGS revealed the presence of K. pneumoniae (225 unique reads) without drug resistance genes.
In case 2, the mNGS test revealed the presence of K. pneumoniae after 16 hours while blood culture showed CrKP after 4 days.
Cerebrospinal fluid was detected by mNGS, and Aspergillus flavus (62 unique reads) and cytomegalovirus (218 unique reads) were detected, while the culture was negative.
After treatment, the patient's body temperature and blood pressure returned to normal.

36531828.exclusion_reason: Case report (n=2 patients); no 2x2, no denominator.

37541984.citation: Shen Zaihong, Wang Ying, Bao Aihua, et al. Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing for Pathogens in Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid Improves the Survival of Patients with Pulmonary Complications after Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation. Infectious Diseases and Therapy, 2023.
37541984.study_design: Prospective single-center study (registered NCT04051372); authors also call it 'single-center retrospective study' in limitations

population.population_description: 134 pulmonary complication cases in 101 patients after allo-HSCT who underwent bronchoscopy with BALF mNGS and conventional tests
population.haemato_subtypes: AML 44, MDS 18, ALL 16, lymphoma 13, CMML 6, mixed lineage leukemia 2, aplastic anemia 1, myelofibrosis 1

37541984.neutropenic_status: Not reported as a stratification variable

specimens.type: BALF/sputum conventional tests (culture, GM, BDG, PCR for CMV/EBV/TB)

index_test.platform_or_panel: unbiased mNGS, DNA library, NCBI microbial databases (4945 viral, 6350 bacterial, 1064 fungal, 234 parasitic genomes); positivity threshold SDSMRN >= 3

37541984.reference_standard: Comprehensive clinical diagnosis: two hematologists (plus respiratory physician for disagreement) reviewed clinical manifestations, chest radiology, laboratory and microbiological tests and treatment response to adjudicate causative pathogens

diagnostic_yield.basis: Diagnostic performance of mNGS vs comprehensive clinical diagnosis (all cases): sensitivity 80.99% (72.63-87.33), specificity 61.54% (32.28-84.87), PPV 95.15% (88.50-98.20), NPV 25.81% (12.54-44.93); PJ: sensitivity 100%, specificity 99.12%; virus sensitivity 93.94%, fungi (excl PJ) sensitivity 36%; 99 strains mNGS 'false positive' per clinical diagnosis, 30 'false negative'. Raw TP/FP/FN/TN counts not published.

37541984.additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS detected more pathogens than conventional tests (266 vs 120 strains); sensitivity 80.99% vs 59.50% (P<0.001); PJ detection rate 8.27% (22/266) by mNGS vs 1.67% (2/120) by conventional (P=0.013)
37541984.therapy_change: Antibiotic coverage narrowed in 32 cases, broadened in 47, maintained in 15 (of 134 cases, per mNGS results and clinical diagnosis)
37541984.mortality_or_outcomes: Overall mortality 17.82% (18/101), pulmonary-complication mortality 10.89% (11/101); 6-month OS 88.89% in early-mNGS group (<=7 days, n=72) vs 65.52% late group (>7 days, n=29) (HR 0.287, 95% CI 0.101-0.819, P=0.006); NRM 9.72% vs 27.59% (P=0.019)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Same BALF specimen used for mNGS and conventional tests; mNGS results were part of the material reviewed for the composite clinical reference standard (potential incorporation bias); multiple BALs per patient (134 episodes/101 patients)

37541984.quadas2_notes: Reference standard is composite clinical adjudication that itself included mNGS results (incorporation bias, index test result known to adjudicators). Raw 2x2 counts not reported, only derived sensitivity/specificity with CIs.

evidence_quotes.quote: From August 2019 to June 2021, a prospective study was performed to comparatively analyze the pathogenic results of mNGS and conventional tests for bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from 134 cases involving 101 patients with pulmonary complications after allo-HSCT.

Two hematologists independently reviewed the medical records of all cases including clinical manifestations, chest radiology, laboratory tests, microbiological tests (conventional tests and mNGS), and treatment response. The causative pathogens of pulmonary infection were determined according to the comprehensive clinical characteristics and available literature.
In this study, mNGS performance better with detection of more pathogens (266 vs 120) and higher sensitivity (80.99% vs 59.50%, P < 0.001) than conventional tests

Among the pathogens detected by mNGS (n = 266), 99 strains were considered as “false positive” results according to clinical diagnosis, which virus accounted for 89.90% (89/99) (Table S3); 30 strains of pathogens were considered “false negative” by mNGS
the antibiotic coverage was narrowed for 32 cases, broadened for 47 cases, while the original antibiotic coverage was maintained for 15 cases (Table S8)

The 6-month overall survival (OS) of 88.89% in the early group was significantly higher than that of 65.52% (HR 0.287, 95% CI 0.101–0.819, P = 0.006) in the late group, while no-relapse mortality (NRM) of 9.72% was significantly lower than that of 27.59% (HR 0.313, 95% CI 0.099–0.986, P = 0.019)
The overall mortality was 17.82% (18/101) and the mortality of pulmonary complications was 10.89% (11/101).

As for PJ, both the sensitivity (100%) and specificity (99.12%) of mNGS were very high, while the sensitivity (9.52%) of conventional tests was very low, although the specificity (100%) was very high.

37541984.exclusion_reason: Sensitivity/specificity vs composite clinical diagnosis reported but raw TP/FP/FN/TN counts not published; cannot reconstruct exact 2x2 without assumptions.

population.population_description: Febrile allo-HSCT recipients with suspected infection; 271 paired mNGS/CMT samples, 258 samples analyzed after excluding 13 paired samples from the same febrile event

37780852.neutropenic_status: Samples grouped by neutropenic status at sampling: cohort A neutropenia n=92 samples, cohort B non-neutropenia n=179 samples

specimens.type: other (lung biopsy 2, urine 1, mucosal secretions 2, pleural effusion 2)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS; positivity: bacteria/fungi SMRN >=3 at species level + genus relative abundance >30%; viruses SMRN >=3; parasites SMRN >=100

37780852.reference_standard: Independent clinical committee (two hematologists, one pulmonologist, one radiologist) adjudicated final diagnosis (clinically significant infection / infection without clinical significance / immune events / mixed) from symptoms, radiology, CMT and treatment response

comparator_2x2.against: conventional microbiological tests (CMT: smear, culture, G test, GM test, PCR for CMV/EBV etc.) - mNGS result vs CMT positivity, all 258 samples

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS positive detection rate 76.4% vs CMT 43.8% (P<0.001). Versus clinical reference standard (clinically significant infection): mNGS sensitivity 81.1%, specificity 56.5%, PPV 80.7%, NPV 57.4% (all 258 samples); blood specimen mNGS sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 52.6%; combination protocol sensitivity 88.3%

37780852.additional_yield_vs_conventional: Of 30 CMT-negative infected cases in cohort A, mNGS matched final causative pathogens in 20 (10 bacterial, 2 fungal, 5 viral, 3 polymicrobial); in cohort B mNGS verified 7 bacterial, 3 fungal, 26 viral, 5 polymicrobial infections in CMT-negative infected patients; P. jirovecii detected only by mNGS; 13/14 Aspergillus cases detected via mNGS vs 1 via CMT
37780852.therapy_change: Treatment success rate of targeted anti-infection strategy 85% (34/40) when based on mNGS vs 56.5% (26/46) with empirical therapy (P=0.004) in the 86 reviewed patients

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Paired mNGS/CMT from same specimens; mNGS results part of adjudication material (incorporation risk); multiple samples per patient (258 samples/153 patients, non-independent)

37780852.quadas2_notes: 2x2 extracted from Table 3 (mNGS vs CMT, total specimens n=258: CMT+/mNGS+ 90, CMT+/mNGS- 23, CMT-/mNGS+ 94, CMT-/mNGS- 51). Note this 2x2 is against CMT positivity, not the clinical reference standard; against clinical diagnosis only sensitivity/specificity are given without raw counts.

evidence_quotes.quote: We performed mNGS and CMT on samples obtained from 153 patients with suspected infection during allo-HSCT. ... we included 271 samples with parallel results for mNGS and CMT from 153 participants.

We retrospectively analyzed the medical records of patients who received allo-HSCT at Ruijin Hospital, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University, and Liquan Hospital, GoBroad Medical Institute of Hematology (Shanghai Center) from April 2021 to January 2023.
The positive detection rate of mNGS was 76.4%, significantly higher than 43.8% of CMT (P<0.001).
our results showed that the sensitivity of mNGS (81.1%) was significantly higher than that of CMT (53.6%) for clinical infection requiring intervention.
We divided these samples into two cohorts based on neutropenic status at the time of sampling: cohort A (neutropenia [n=92]) and cohort B (non-neutropenia [n=179])
The most frequent mNGS sampling specimen was peripheral blood (78.2%), followed by BALF (10.7%), CSF (8.5%), and others (2.6%).
The overall treatment success rate (TSR) was 85% (34/40) for patients treated based on the mNGS results, and 56.5% for those receiving empirical therapy (26/46, P=0.004
Immune events were diagnosed in 57.4% (35/61) of the febrile events with negative mNGS results, and 33.5% (48/143) with negative CMT results (P=0.002).

37985857.citation: Qi Yan, Lin Wu-Qiang, Liao Bin, et al. Blood plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing for identifying pathogens of febrile neutropenia in acute leukemia patients. Scientific Reports, 2023.

population.population_description: Acute leukemia patients with febrile neutropenia (temperature >38.3°C or twice >38.0°C >1h and neutrophil count <500/mm3) undergoing paired plasma mNGS and blood culture within 24 h

37985857.neutropenic_status: FN definition: 'oral temperature > 38.3 °C or twice consecutive > 38.0 °C for more than 1 h and neutrophil count < 500/mm3'

index_test.platform_or_panel: plasma cfDNA mNGS on MGISEQ-2000 (MGI); Genskey kits; ~12,000-genome SNAP database

37985857.reference_standard: Final clinical diagnosis of infectious pathogen at discharge: 'The final diagnosis of the infectious pathogen at the time of discharge was the gold standard', based on comprehensive judgment of three experienced senior physicians

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS diagnostic positivity 25/37 (67.6%) vs blood culture 7/37 (18.9%) (p<0.05). Versus final clinical diagnosis in blood samples: sensitivity 100.00%, specificity 40.00%, PPV 28.00%, NPV 100.00%; agreement of mNGS and BC 51.35% (19/37). Of 14 clinically approved pathogens, 9 detected only by mNGS and 5 by both mNGS and BC. Raw 2x2 counts not published (PPV 28% of 25 mNGS-positives implies 7 TP; not explicitly stated).

37985857.additional_yield_vs_conventional: Of 37 infections, 6 (16.22%) diagnosed by both BC and mNGS, 18 (48.65%) by mNGS only, 12 (32.43%) negative by both; mNGS detected 9 of 14 final pathogens that BC missed

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Same blood draw split for BC and mNGS; clinicians adjudicating final diagnosis were not blinded to mNGS results (incorporation bias); paper has internal inconsistencies (6+18=24 vs reported 25 mNGS-positive patients)

37985857.quadas2_notes: Sensitivity/specificity reported vs discharge clinical diagnosis but no raw TP/FP/FN/TN counts; derived counts would be inconsistent (PPV 28% x 25 = 7 TP, but '6 diagnosed by both BC and mNGS' and sensitivity 100% + NPV 100% constraints do not reconcile cleanly), so no 2x2 built. Note text/figure counting discrepancies.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively reviewed 37 AL patients with FN and compared the results of mNGS with blood culture (BC) and the clinical features of the mNGS-positive group and the mNGS-negative group.
From February 2020 to February 2023, a total of 37 AL patients with FN were enrolled in the Affiliated People's Hospital of Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
The diagnostic positivity rate of mNGS (25/37, 67.6%) was significantly higher than that of BC (7/37, 18.9%), and the difference was statistically significant (p < 0.05).
The sensitivity and specificity were 100.00% and 40.00%, respectively. The positive prediction value (PPV) and negative prediction value (NPV) were 28.00% and 100.00%, respectively.
Of 37 infections, 6 (16.22%) were diagnosed by both BC and mNGS, 18 (48.65%) by mNGS only, and 12 (32.43%) were negative by both BC and mNGS
A total of 14 detected pathogens were the final clinical diagnosis, of which 9 strains were detected only by mNGS and 5 strains were detected by both mNGS and BC.
The final diagnosis of the infectious pathogen at the time of discharge was the gold standard.
meeting the criteria for FN: oral temperature > 38.3 °C or twice consecutive > 38.0 °C for more than 1 h and neutrophil count < 500/mm3

37985857.exclusion_reason: No raw 2x2 counts; derived counts internally inconsistent; n=37 modest.

evidence_quotes.quote: A total of 153 hematology patients with suspected infection who underwent mNGS using plasma were enrolled in the study. ... From October 2020 to July 2023, we screened all patients who underwent mNGS with plasma at the Department of Hematology, West China Hospital.

In 153 plasma samples, mNGS yielded a higher positivity rate than CMT (total: 88.24% vs. 40.52%, P<0.001; bacteria: 35.95% vs. 21.57%, P < 0.01; virus: 69.93% vs. 21.57%, P<0.001; fungi: 20.26% vs. 7.84%, P<0.01).
Neutropenia was defined as an absolute neutrophil count <500/μL or <1000/μL with a high probability of decrease <500/μL in the next 2 days.

Of these patients, 141 (92.16%) had been treated with chemotherapy, ... 52 (33.99%) with hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT). At the time of the mNGS test, 47.06% (72/153) of the patients had neutropenia. ... The majority of patients (150/153, 98.04%) were exposed to antibiotics prior to sampling. The 28-day mortality rate was 29.41% (45/153).
In our 153 cases, 76 cases (76/153, 49.67%) were positive for mNGS and negative for CMT, and 3 cases (3/153, 1.96%) were positive for CMT and negative for mNGS.

Overall, 51 (33.33%) were antibiotic adjusted by mNGS, and 102 (66.67%) were not adjusted. ... The antibiotic adjustment rate was higher in the neutropenia group than in the non-neutropenia group (45.83% vs. 22.22%, P < 0.01)

both the 3-day and 7-day efficacy rates in the HSCT group were higher than those in the non-HSCT group (3-day: 82.22% vs. 58.65%, P < 0.01; 7-day: 88.89% vs. 67.31%, P < 0.01), and the 28-day mortality rate was lower in the HSCT group than in the non-HSCT group (6.67% vs. 38.89%, P < 0.000).
When CMT was used as the reference standard, the sensitivity and specificity of mNGS were 62.5% (95% CI: 48.5%-74.8%) and 17.53% (95% CI: 10.8%-26.9%), respectively.

The clinical diagnosis was aplastic anemia in five cases, myelodysplastic syndromes in five cases, leukemia in 10 cases, lymphoma in two cases, myeloma in two cases, myelofibrosis in four cases, and other diseases in four cases.

41327021.citation: Chen B, Shu W, Le J, Jin D. Application of metagenomic next-generation sequencing technology in hematologic malignancy patients with sepsis following antibiotic use. BMC Infectious Diseases. 2025;25:1678.
41327021.study_design: Retrospective single-centre analysis of haematological-malignancy patients with sepsis after >=3 days of antibiotics without improvement

population.population_description: All 119 patients had haematological malignancies with sepsis (Sepsis-3) after >=3 days antibiotic therapy without clinical improvement; 58 (48.73%) had antitumor-therapy-related neutropenia/granulocytopenia. No transplant subgroup reported.
population.haemato_subtypes: Lymphoma 58 (48.73%), multiple myeloma 32 (26.89%), acute leukemia 29 (24.36%).

41327021.neutropenic_status: 58 patients (48.73%) developed neutropenia as a result of antitumor therapy (post-chemotherapy myelosuppression/drug-induced granulocytopenia); no ANC threshold quoted in main text (neutropenia defined by reference [16])

specimens.type: peripheral blood (plasma for mNGS; paired blood culture)

index_test.platform_or_panel: Blood/plasma mNGS: Genewiz NGSmaster(TM) automated workflow, library prep with Genewiz bloodstream infection kit, Illumina Nextseq550, 50-bp single-end; Gentellix bioinformatics vs NCBI GenBank + Genewiz internal database
index_test.commercial_or_inhouse: Commercial (Genewiz / Hangzhou Matridx Biotechnology Co., Ltd.)
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: Both DNA and RNA (simultaneous reverse transcription; though limitations state RNA virus detection was not included)

41327021.reference_standard: Paired blood culture (targeting bacteria and fungi) used as comparator; no independent final-diagnosis reference standard (culture was the 'gold standard' comparator). Sepsis defined per Sepsis-3.

comparator_2x2.against: Blood culture (bacteria and fungi) in the 47 patients with fungal and/or bacterial infection identified by either method

diagnostic_yield.basis: Among 47 patients with fungal and/or bacterial infection, mNGS positive in 42 (89.36%) vs blood culture positive in 12 (25.53%).

41327021.additional_yield_vs_conventional: 35 cases (74.46%) exclusively mNGS-positive, 5 cases (10.64%) only culture-positive, 7 (14.90%) dual positive; mNGS identified more bacterial (42 vs 11) and fungal (16 vs 1) pathogens than culture; polymicrobial infection detection 25.00% vs 0.00% (P<0.001).
41327021.therapy_change: Anti-infective treatment regimens modified based on blood mNGS results in 47 patients (39.49%); 18 cases (15.12%) continued initial therapy.
41327021.mortality_or_outcomes: 30-day mortality 18/119 (15.12%): lymphoma 8/58 (~13.79%), acute leukemia 7/29 (~24.14%), multiple myeloma 3/32 (~9.38%); neutropenic (observation) group 12/58 (20.69%) vs non-neutropenic control 6/61 (9.84%), P=0.099. Fever resolution 83.19%, septic shock improvement 40.00%.

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Only patients positive by EITHER blood culture or mNGS were included (inclusion criterion 3), so true test-negatives are excluded by design; the 2x2 is built on this enriched subset (TN=0 by construction), severely biasing accuracy estimates.

41327021.quadas2_notes: Patient selection: enrichment for culture- or mNGS-positive patients makes the 2x2 non-generalisable (specificity 0.00% and NPV 0.00% are artefacts of including only patients positive by either test). Index test well described (platform, QC, cutoffs not fully specified). Reference standard: blood culture alone, compromised by prior antibiotics >=3 days in all patients; incorporation/culture-bias concerns. Reported kappa inconsistent (-0.202 vs -0.229) and agreement 13.21% corresponds to 7/53 not 7/47 - internal inconsistency. Verbatim table 2 values used for the 2x2; reconstructed from the garbled table text, consistent with sensitivity 58.33% (7/12), specificity 0.00% (0/35), PPV 16.67% (7/42), NPV 0.00% (0/5).

Patients with hematologic malignancies presented to the Department of Hematology with fever and clinical signs of infection, and had positive results by either blood culture or mNGS, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for definite sepsis

For the detection of bacterial and fungal pathogens, mNGS demonstrated a significantly higher positive rate compared to blood culture (89.36% vs. 25.53%). The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of mNGS were 58.33%, 0.00%, 16.67%, and 0.00%, respectively. The overall agreement rate between the two methods was 13.21% (kappa = -0.202).

Among them, 58 patients (48.73%) developed neutropenia [16] as a result of antitumor therapy.

41645073.citation: Xu C, Zhang L, Liu T, Zhu G, Wei H, Zheng Y, et al. Respiratory and blood samples metagenomic sequencing in diagnosing pulmonary infections in hematologic patients. BMC Infectious Diseases. 2026;26:514.
41645073.study_design: Retrospective single-centre cohort (Institute of Hematology and Blood Diseases Hospital, Tianjin); paired blood-mNGS and LRTS-mNGS

population.population_description: 160 cases (156 patients enrolled; 151 cases/147 patients analyzed after excluding uncertain etiology) with haematological disorders and suspected pulmonary infection who underwent both blood-mNGS and LRTS-mNGS within one week. HSCT recipients: 51/127 BFPI cases (40.2%) had HSCT (47 allo, 4 auto).
population.haemato_subtypes: Analyzed cases (N=147 patients): AML 44.2% (65/147), ALL 17.7% (26/147), lymphoma 15.0% (22/147). In BFPI cases (N=127): AML 54 (42.5%), ALL 24 (18.9%), lymphoma 19 (15.0%), MDS 11 (8.7%), aplastic anemia 7 (5.5%), other 12 (9.4%).

41645073.neutropenic_status: Neutropenia reported as neutropenic phase: 30.5% (46/151) of cases; 37/127 (29.1%) BFPI cases neutropenic (Table 1); blood-mNGS PPA stratified by neutropenia (21/37 vs 23/90). ANC median reported (1.78 x 10^9/L IQR 0.37-3.63 in BFPI cases) but ANC cut-off defining neutropenia not stated in main text

specimens.type: lower respiratory tract samples: BALF 90 (56.3%) + sputum 70 (43.8%) (mNGS)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS (blood and LRTS); workflow described in prior publications and supplementary methods; 7 AMR markers targeted (mecA, blaOXA-23, blaOXA-48, blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMP)
index_test.commercial_or_inhouse: partly commercial (Tianjin Union Precision Medical Diagnostic Co., Ltd.)

41645073.reference_standard: Clinical composite diagnosis (CCD) by an expert panel (microbiologist, radiologist, two hematologists, chaired by senior hematologist) based on all laboratory results (including mNGS and CMT), clinical presentation, imaging, antimicrobial adjustments and outcomes; pulmonary infection per CDC/NHSN surveillance definitions. Also compared against CMT.

comparator_2x2.against: Clinical composite diagnosis (CCD) for bacterial/fungal pulmonary infection; blood-mNGS (LRTS-mNGS 2x2 also given: TP 119, FP 3, FN 8, TN 21). Vs CMT: blood-mNGS 27/19/47/58; LRTS-mNGS 68/6/62/1.

diagnostic_yield.basis: LRTS-mNGS detected pulmonary pathogens in 119/127 (93.7%) BFPI cases vs blood-mNGS 44/127 (34.6%).

41645073.additional_yield_vs_conventional: In 7 cases pathogens (all fungi) were detected only by blood-mNGS (2 Aspergillus spp., 1 Mucorales, 1 Pneumocystis spp. single infections; plus 3 mixed infections with additional fungi detected); in 10 cases pathogens detected only by CMT. Total genera detected: LRTS-mNGS 189/207 (91.3%), CMT 81/207 (39.1%), blood-mNGS 58/207 (28.0%).
41645073.turnaround_time: described as short in introduction; no specific hours/days reported in main text
41645073.therapy_change: mNGS positively influenced antimicrobial adjustments in 54.3% (69/127) of cases; negative impact in 1 case (0.8%); most common positive impact was addition of agents to target previously uncovered pathogens (37/69, 53.6%).
41645073.mortality_or_outcomes: 28-day mortality: 21/127 (16.5%) in BFPI cases, 3/24 (12.5%) in viral/non-infectious cases (Table 1).

quality_flags.blinding_of_index_result: unclear (expert panel had access to all results including mNGS - incorporation into CCD)
quality_flags.overlap_risk: CCD incorporates mNGS results, so mNGS-vs-CCD agreement overestimates true accuracy; CMT-referenced 2x2 provided as alternative. Retrospective, clinician-driven (non-consecutive) test ordering.

41645073.quadas2_notes: Excellent paired design (blood and LRTS within one week, same patients). Reference standard (CCD) includes mNGS -> incorporation bias in the CCD-referenced 2x2; the CMT-referenced 2x2 is also reported. Index test positive-reporting criteria in supplementary/previous publications only. Flow: 184 screened -> 156 patients/160 cases (4 incomplete records, 24 without CMT excluded); 9 uncertain-etiology cases excluded from accuracy analysis. Blood-mNGS false negatives dominate (83/127 vs CCD), while LRTS-mNGS dominates sensitivity.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed 184 patients with suspected pulmonary infections who underwent mNGS testing of blood and LRTS (with the two samples collected within one week of each other) in the Institute of Hematology and Blood Diseases Hospital from March 2021 to March 2024 (Fig. 1). ... After excluding 4 patients with incomplete medical records and 24 patients without CMT, a total of 156 patients (involving 160 cases and 320 mNGS tests) were finally enrolled.
Compared with CCD, the PPA of blood-mNGS and LRTS-mNGS was 34.6% (44/127) and 93.7% (119/127), respectively, while the NPA was 91.7% (22/24) and 87.5% (21/24)

The clinical composite diagnosis (CCD) was determined based on all laboratory test results, including both mNGS and CMT, along with clinical presentation, imaging findings, antimicrobial adjustments, and patient outcomes.

Importantly, in 7 cases, pathogens were only detected by blood-mNGS, all of which were fungi. Among these, 4 involved single fungal infections (2 caused by Aspergillus spp, 1 caused by Mucorales, and 1 by Pneumocystis spp.), while 3 were mixed fungal infections in which blood-mNGS identified additional fungal pathogens (2 Mucorales, and 1 both Mucorales and Aspergillus spp.) not detected by other methods.
The numbers of genera detected by LRTS-mNGS, CTM and blood-mNGS were 189 (91.3%, 189/207), 81 (39.1%, 81/207), 58 (28.0%, 58/207), respectively.
Additionally, the PPA of blood-mNGS was significantly higher in patients with neutropenia compared to those without [56.8% (21/37) vs. 25.6% (23/90), P = 0.001]
In terms of clinical value for antimicrobial adjustment, mNGS provided a positive impact in 69 out of 127 cases (54.3%), while only 1 case (0.8%) showed a negative impact.

The most common underlying conditions were acute myeloid leukemia (44.2%, 65/147), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (17.7%, 26/147), and lymphoma (15.0%, 22/147). Among the 151 cases, 30.5% (46/151) were in the neutropenic phase, and 80.8% (122/151) had been exposed to antimicrobial agents prior to undergoing mNGS testing
The LRTS included 90 (56.3%) BALF samples and 70 (43.8%) sputum samples.

41660499.citation: Hensley MK, Sayed K, Haidar G, Wang X, Benos PV, Ito S, et al. Rapid Metagenomic Sequencing of Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid for Diagnosis of Infection in Patients With Hematologic Malignancies and Pulmonary Complications. CHEST Pulmonary. 2025;3(4):100173.
41660499.study_design: Prospective proof-of-concept observational cohort (RaMSeS), single centre (University of Pittsburgh)

population.population_description: 30 adult inpatients with hematologic malignancy and pulmonary complications (hypoxemia or new/worsening radiographic abnormality) undergoing clinical diagnostic bronchoscopy; 10/30 (33.3%) had prior hematopoietic cell transplant.
population.haemato_subtypes: AML 13 (43.3%); prior HCT 10 (33.3%). Clinical consensus groups: bacterial LRTI 4, viral LRTI 4, fungal LRTI 9, mixed LRTI 5, noninfectious PC 8.

41660499.neutropenic_status: Neutropenia defined as absolute neutrophil count < 500 cells/μL in the week before bronchoscopy: 18/30 (60.0%)

specimens.type: bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (research aliquots; >=10 mL from same lobe as clinical BAL)

index_test.platform_or_panel: Two assays: 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq, bacterial only) and Nanopore metagenomic long-read sequencing (Oxford Nanopore MinION Mk1c, saponin-based human DNA depletion); threshold >=50 microbial reads
index_test.commercial_or_inhouse: Inhouse (research, University of Pittsburgh Center for Medicine and the Microbiome)
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA only (16S: bacteria; Nanopore: bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi)

41660499.reference_standard: Clinical consensus classification by 3 physicians integrating CMT results (culture/PCR/antigen), imaging, clinical course and treatment response; fungal LRTI per EORTC/MSG criteria; CMT itself used for concordance comparisons. No independent validated reference standard.

diagnostic_yield.basis: No single overall mNGS positivity rate reported. CMT identified plausible LRT pathogens in 16/30 (53%). 16S-Seq: positive concordance with CMT 4/6 (66.7%), negative concordance 3/7 (42.9%), additional plausible pathogens in 16/27 (59.3%). Nanopore: positive concordance 1/15 (6.7%), negative concordance 7/8 (87.5%), additional pathogens in 11/26 (42.3%).

41660499.additional_yield_vs_conventional: 16S-Seq identified additional plausible respiratory pathogens in 16/27 (59.3%) patients; Nanopore in 11/26 (42.3%). Per group: 16S additive yield bacterial LRTI 3/4, mixed 3/4, viral 3/4, fungal 5/8, noninfectious 2/7; Nanopore 2/3, 2/3, 2/4, 4/8, 1/8. Nanopore detected no abundant pathogenic fungal species in the 9 fungal LRTIs.
41660499.turnaround_time: Nanopore real-time sequencing capable of species-level ID 'as early as 6 to 8 hours' (cited as general capability, not measured in study); no measured TAT reported
41660499.mortality_or_outcomes: Respiratory failure 23/30 (76.7%), ICU transfer 15/30 (50.0%), mechanical ventilation 10/30 (33.3%), death within 30 days of bronchoscopy 10/30 (33.3%); median length of stay 17 days (IQR 4-39).

quality_flags.overlap_risk: No full 2x2: Nanopore comparisons exclude 4 cases with >=99% human DNA; 3 16S samples unavailable; concordance denominators vary by subset (e.g. positive concordance 4/6 of 16 CMT-positive). Clinical consensus classification partially relies on CMT, and sequencing results were not used to define groups - limited incorporation risk but denominators incomplete.

41660499.quadas2_notes: Small proof-of-concept (n=30). No full 2x2 reconstructible from main text (e-Tables not available in XML); concordance reported only over analysable subsets with variable denominators. Index test: two distinct research assays, inhouse, no clinical validation thresholds. Reference standard: retrospective 3-physician consensus, subjective, CMT-based with limited sensitivity; all patients received antimicrobials before bronchoscopy (differential verification concerns). Nanopore performed poorly for molds (possible pre-analytic host-depletion/extraction artifact per authors).

evidence_quotes.quote: Prospective proof-of-concept cohort study of 30 adult inpatients with hematologic malignancies and PCs who underwent bronchoscopy for suspected lower respiratory tract infection.

We prospectively enrolled adult (≥ 18 years of age) hospitalized patients with HM and a diagnosis of PCs (defined as hypoxemia or new/worsening radiographic abnormality) who underwent clinical diagnostic bronchoscopy from March 1, 2022, to October 30, 2022.

18 (60.0%) were neutropenic (absolute neutrophil count < 500 cells/μL) in the week before bronchoscopy. Thirteen (43.3%) had acute myeloid leukemia, and 10 (33.3%) had prior hematopoietic cell transplantation

In total, CMT identified a pathogen via culture- or polymerase chain reaction-based testing in 53% of patients. 16S-Seq demonstrated 66.7% positive concordance, demonstrated 42.9% negative concordance with CMT, and identified additional plausible respiratory pathogens in 59.3% of patients. Nanopore demonstrated 6.7% positive concordance and 87.5% negative concordance with CMT, and it identified additional plausible respiratory pathogens in 42.3% of patients
Of the 30 cases, 4 (13.3%) had ≥ 99% human DNA by Nanopore and were excluded from further comparisons (e-Table 1, Fig 1). For 16S-Seq, 3 samples (10.0%) were not available due to operational reasons.
Nanopore sequencing did not detect any abundant pathogenic fungal species in these 9 fungal LRTIs. However, C dubliniensis reads were detected in 7 of 9 cases (77.8%)
Clinical consensus classifications (groups) defined 22 patients (73.3%) as having infectious PCs (4 bacterial, 4 viral, 9 fungal, 5 mixed) and 8 patients (26.7%) as having noninfectious PCs

The median length of stay was 17 days (interquartile range, 4-39), 23 (76.7%) developed respiratory failure, 15 (50.0%) required ICU transfer, 10 (33.3%) required mechanical ventilation, and 10 (33.3%) died within 30 days of bronchoscopy.

Nanopore's ability to produce long reads and analyze DNA in real time means that species-level identification and resistance profiling can be achieved in clinically relevant turnaround times, as early as 6 to 8 hours

To address time-related diagnostic limitations, we used a retrospective consensus approach among 3 physicians to integrate clinical and microbiological data. Although our approach represents pragmatic physician diagnostic thinking on available CMT results, it introduces potential subjectivity.

41660499.exclusion_reason: No complete 2x2 vs reference standard or CMT reconstructible (variable, subset denominators; 4 Nanopore and 3 16S cases excluded); concordance/additive-yield data only. n=30 borderline small.

41868021.citation: Zhan M, Tu S, Yang S, Yin Y, Wang Z, Zhang F, et al. Clinical Utility of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing in Diagnosing Central Nervous System Infections in Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: A Retrospective and Prospective Cohort Study. Infection and Drug Resistance. 2026;19:505-482 (Dove Press, doi:10.2147/IDR.S554425).
41868021.study_design: Mixed retrospective and prospective cohort (87 retrospective, 40 prospective), single centre (Peking University People's Hospital)

population.population_description: 127 patients with suspected CNS infection (acute fever >38.5 C plus at least one neurologic sign) undergoing CSF mNGS. Underlying disease: allo-HSCT 70 (55.1%), hematologic malignancies 15 (11.8%), autoimmune disease 11 (8.7%), cerebrovascular disease 5, Guillain-Barre 3, others 7, not applicable elsewhere. N usable by us = 70 allo-HSCT + 15 HM = 85.
population.haemato_subtypes: allo-HSCT 70 (55.1%); hematologic malignancies 15 (11.8%). Pathogens detected in 14/20 positives in allo-HSCT, 3/20 in HM.

index_test.platform_or_panel: In-house CSF mNGS: QIAamp DNA Microbiome Kit extraction, Illumina NextSeq 550Dx, 75-bp single-end, >=20 million reads/sample; Kraken2 taxonomy vs NCBI-derived database; positivity by species-specific RPM ratio (Rr) cutoffs from ROC analysis
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA only (RNA viruses would not be detected; DNA extraction only)

41868021.reference_standard: Composite of conventional methods (culture, ink stain, cryptococcal antigen) OR Sanger sequencing (PCR-based orthogonal confirmation of mNGS/PCR findings); positive = any pathogen identified by conventional methods or Sanger sequencing

comparator_2x2.against: Reference criterion: any pathogen identified by conventional methods or Sanger sequencing (reconstructed from reported sensitivity 82.6% = 19/23, specificity 99.0% = 103/104, mNGS-positive n = 20, mNGS-negative n = 107)

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS positive in 20/127 (15.7%) CSF samples; conventional methods positive in 4/127 (3.1%); Sanger sequencing positive in 19/127 (15.0%).

41868021.additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS detected 20 pathogen-positive samples of which 19 were confirmed by Sanger sequencing; conventional methods detected only 4 positives, and all pathogen-positive samples by Sanger or mNGS were negative by conventional methods except the 4 conventional positives. Four mNGS/Sanger-negative cases were culture/CrAg positive (S. lugdunensis, C. minutissimum, R. marceus, one CrAg+).

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Major incorporation bias: 19 of the 23 reference-positive cases were defined by Sanger sequencing confirmation of mNGS findings, so mNGS effectively contributes to its own reference standard. Only 4 reference positives came from conventional methods.

41868021.quadas2_notes: 2x2 reconstructed from Table 3 (mNGS positive 20/15.7%, negative 107; sensitivity 82.6%, specificity 99.0%, PPV 95.0%, NPV 96.3%) and is internally consistent. Reference standard heavily dependent on Sanger confirmation of mNGS targets - incorporation/verification bias; patients with negative mNGS and negative conventional tests counted as true negatives without clinical follow-up diagnosis. DNA-only panel (misses RNA viruses). Population is mixed (55% allo-HSCT, 12% HM, remainder non-haemato/neurologic), so haemato-stratified accuracy not available. Authors acknowledge non-random selection and reliance on Sanger for the ROC-positive definition.

evidence_quotes.quote: A total of 127 patients with suspected CNSIs were prospectively enrolled for this study between May 2018 and August 2022.

The specificity and sensitivity of mNGS were 99.0% and 82.6%, respectively (Table 3). Conventional methods and Sanger sequencing both demonstrated a specificity of 100.0%, while their sensitivities were 17.4% and 82.6%, respectively (Table 3). Notably, combining mNGS with conventional methods increased sensitivity to 100.0%, while specificity remained at 99.0%.

To evaluate the diagnostic performance of mNGS for pathogen detection in CSF, we established a reference criterion, defining a positive result as any pathogen identified by conventional methods or Sanger sequencing.
Remarkably, mNGS detected 20 pathogen-positive cases, whereas conventional methods identified only four. Furthermore, 19 of the mNGS-positive cases were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

Three samples that tested positive by culture for S. lugdunensis, C. minutissimum, and R. marceu, as well as one CrAg-positive sample from a patient with severe CNSI symptoms, were not detected by mNGS (Supplemental Figure 2) or Sanger sequencing.
The distribution of underlying disease varied significantly between the two cohorts (p <0.001), with allo-HSCT being the predominant condition in the retrospective cohort (64.4%)

The suspicion of CNS infections was based on the presence of acute fever (> 38.5°C) accompanied by at least one of the following clinical signs: (1) stiff neck, (2) altered consciousness, (3) increased anterior fontanelle tension, or (4) meningeal irritation.

Library preparation and sequences were performed using the NextSeq 550Dx High Output Reagent Kit v2.5 (Illumina). A 75-bp single-end sequencing was performed and at least 20 million sequencing reads were obtained for each sample.
Pathogens were most frequently detected in patients who had undergone allo-HSCT (14/20), followed by those with underlying hematological malignancies (HM) (3/20)

41909845.citation: Wang C, Min M, Dai Z, Wang G, Wang Y, Hu T, et al. Diagnostic value of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in patients with febrile lung cancer with negative conventional microbiological tests and without neutropenia. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2026;16:1715563.
41909845.study_design: Single-centre retrospective cohort, consecutive screening (Cancer Center, Union Hospital, Wuhan)

population.population_description: All 53 primary-analysis patients had histologically confirmed LUNG CANCER (solid tumour) with fever and negative conventional microbiological tests; all were non-neutropenic by design (neutropenia was an exclusion criterion). Not a haemato-oncology or transplant population.
population.haemato_subtypes: None - adenocarcinoma 27 (50.9%), squamous cell carcinoma 21 (39.6%), small-cell lung cancer 4 (7.5%), other 1 (1.9%).

41909845.neutropenic_status: Non-neutropenic by design: neutropenia excluded, defined as ANC < 0.5 x 10^9/L within -24 to +24 h of fever onset

specimens.type: plasma (EDTA whole blood 5-10 mL, cell-free DNA)

index_test.platform_or_panel: PMseq (BGI, Shenzhen) plasma cfDNA shotgun mNGS on Illumina or MGISEQ platforms; PMDB database (~17,500 taxa); >=20 million reads/sample; RPM thresholds plus enrichment over negative controls

41909845.reference_standard: None - no independent gold standard; patients classified into mNGS-positive high-suspicion infectious fever (n=37) vs mNGS-negative high-suspicion tumor fever (n=16) based on mNGS results plus clinical adjudication (explicitly acknowledged limitation)

diagnostic_yield.basis: Among 53 CMT-negative patients, plasma mNGS identified >=1 pathogen in 37 (69.8%); 54 pathogen detections total (18 bacterial, 28 viral, 8 fungal).

41909845.additional_yield_vs_conventional: All 53 patients were CMT-negative (blood cultures within <=24 h plus limited viral/atypical serology); mNGS was positive in 37 (69.8%) of them. No paired CMT comparison possible because CMT was uniformly negative and the conventional panel was limited (acknowledged by authors).
41909845.turnaround_time: Defined as time from laboratory receipt to report availability; stated to be reported as median (IQR) but no numeric TAT value appears in the main text
41909845.therapy_change: mNGS-positive reports prompted immediate result-guided antimicrobial adjustments (institutional practice); mNGS-negative cases continued oncological/supportive care without escalation. No counts reported.
41909845.mortality_or_outcomes: No mortality reported; defervescence by 48 h post-t0: 73.0% (27/37) mNGS-positive vs 37.5% (6/16) mNGS-negative, p=0.029; by 96 h 89.2% (33/37) vs 68.8% (11/16), p=0.027; log-rank p=0.025, unadjusted HR 2.08 (95% CI 1.09-3.97).

quality_flags.blinding_of_index_result: no (group assignment and management tied directly to mNGS result)
quality_flags.overlap_risk: mNGS result itself defines the classification (HSIF vs HSTF) - circular design; no independent reference standard; confounding by indication and guarantee-time bias acknowledged by authors.

41909845.quadas2_notes: WRONG POPULATION for this review: febrile lung cancer (solid tumour), non-neutropenic by design, no haematologic malignancy or HSCT patients. No 2x2 vs any reference standard (authors state interpretation 'is limited by the retrospective design and lack of an independent gold standard'). Retrospective, single-centre, 212 screened -> 87 analysed -> 53 CMT-negative (125 excluded mostly for incomplete data). Not usable for pooled diagnostic-accuracy analysis in haemato-oncology mNGS review.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed the results of whole blood mNGS testing from 231 blood samples of hematological disorders patients with suspected infections.
Between June 2022 and March 2024, a total of 302 individuals who underwent whole blood mNGS testing were screened, of whom 231 met the inclusion criteria were included in the final analysis.

Among the 231 enrolled patients, whole blood mNGS yielded a positive rate of 77.06%, which was significantly higher than that of blood culture (BC) (21.65%, P < 0.001), but no significantly different from plasma mNGS (72.29%, P = 0.285) or CMT (82.68%, P = 0.132)

Using the final clinical diagnosis as the reference standard, whole blood mNGS achieved the highest sensitivity, 81.73%, followed by plasma mNGS (76.44%), CMT (45.19%) and BC (23.56%). BC had the highest specificity, 100%, followed by whole blood mNGS and plasma mNGS (both 86.96%). Whole blood mNGS also demonstrated a higher positive predictive value (PPV, 98.27%) and negative predictive value (NPV, 34.43%) compared with the other methods

Based on the final clinical assessment, 90.04% (208/231) of the patients were diagnosed with infection and were classified into the infection group, while the remaining 9.96% (23/231) were classified as the non-infected group.

The final clinical diagnosis of infection was evaluated by two supervising clinicians based on the composite reference standard: combined results of all microbiological tests, radiological testing results, and a summary of the patient clinical examining results and symptoms.

A total of 107 clinically relevant microorganisms were identified across all patients by whole blood mNGS, BC and CMT (including BC), comprising 69 bacterial species (including 3 atypical pathogens), 24 fungal species, 12 viral species, and two parasitic species. Whole blood mNGS demonstrated superior detection capability, identifying 101 of the 107 total species (94.4%). When whole blood mNGS was partitioned into its plasma and cellular components, plasma mNGS detected 88 species (82.2%), while an additional 13 clinically relevant microorganisms (12.1%) were identified exclusively in the blood cell fraction
The turnaround time (from sample receipt to report generation) for mNGS testing ranged between 15 and 20 h, with a median of 17.5 h.
Whole blood mNGS demonstrated the highest proportion of positive influence (72.73%), surpassing plasma mNGS (68.40%), CMT (incorporating BC, 37.66%), and BC (18.61%).
The in-hospital mortality rate was 19.05% (44/231), with a median length of hospital stay of 26 days (IQR 14–37.5)

The majority had hematologic malignancies, primarily acute myeloid leukemia (AML, 48.48%, 112/231), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL, 18.18%, 42/231), and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS, 16.02%, 37/231). Overall, 64.07% (148/231) underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and 98.27% (227/231) were immunosuppressed.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study enrolled 96 pediatric patients who developed diarrhea following HSCT for hematologic malignancies at Children's Hospital of Soochow University between March 2023 and October 2025. A total of 185 feces collected during diarrheal episodes were subjected to mNGS analysis.
A total of 109 cases were positive for mNGS but negative for CMT, 29 cases were positive for both mNGS and CMT, and 40 cases were negative for both (Figure 1A).
Panel A is a pie chart displaying the distribution of cases among four groups—mNGS+CMT- (blue, 109), mNGS+CMT+ (orange, 29), mNGS-CMT- (yellow, 40), and mNGS-CMT+ (green, 7).

Due to the absence of standardized criteria for interpreting mNGS results in this clinical context, and given that our proposed classification framework would likely categorize a substantial proportion of cases as true positives, we refrained from interpreting the sensitivity and specificity of NGS in this study.

Among the pathogens detected by mNGS in the 185 fecal samples, the predominant bacteria were Pseudomonas spp. (28 cases), Clostridioides spp. (28 cases), Campylobacter spp. (25 cases), Acinetobacter spp. (16 cases), and Staphylococcus aureus (13 cases). Regarding viruses, Adenovirus (47 cases), Polyomavirus (34 cases), Cytomegalovirus (8 cases)and Norovirus (7 cases) were the most prevalent

Among the 142 pathogen-positive specimens, single bacterial infections were identified in 29 cases, including 26 Gram-negative bacteria and 3 Gram-positive bacteria. Single viral infections were identified in 37 cases, including 34 DNA viruses and 3 RNA viruses. Co-infections included 33 cases of multiple bacteria, 43 cases of bacterial-viral co-infection
The primary types of hematologic diseases were Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML), Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia and Aplastic Anemia (AA).
A total of 91.67% of pediatric patients improved, 4 cases were discharged against medical advice, and 4 cases were not cured. The average length of hospital stay was 33.68 days (range: 6–70 days)
